extracted.intended_audience: individual researchers (independent scholars; faculty and staff at institutions of higher education) preparing applications for the NEH Summer Stipends 2024 competition
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing and submitting an application for the National Endowment for the Humanities (NEH) Summer Stipends program to support two consecutive months of full-time humanities research and writing. Includes eligibility, required documents, formatting, review criteria, and post-award obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review Criterion 1: Intellectual significance
rubrics_metrics.description: The intellectual significance of the proposed project, including its value to humanities scholars, general audiences, or both.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer reviewers evaluate the project's thesis/claim, basic ideas, problems or questions examined, and how the project complements, challenges, or expands relevant studies in the field. Address in the Narrative under 'Significance and contribution.' NEH gives preference to projects providing free public access to results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review Criterion 2: Quality of conception and clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: The quality of the conception, definition, organization, and description of the project and the applicant’s clarity of expression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain project organization and methods in the Narrative under 'Organization and methods.' For books provide chapter outline if possible; for articles provide argument overview, sources, and word count; for digital projects describe technologies; for editions/translations describe annotations and rationale for new translations. Clarity matters because reviewers are not necessarily specialists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review Criterion 3: Feasibility and plan of work
rubrics_metrics.description: The feasibility and appropriateness of the proposed plan of work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the one-page Work plan to show major activities, timeline, and that you will work full-time for two consecutive months. NEH will primarily consider work plan under criterion 3. Avoid plans heavily dependent on factors outside applicant control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review Criterion 4: Applicant competence and promise
rubrics_metrics.description: The quality or promise of quality of the applicant as an interpreter of the humanities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Résumé (2 pages) to demonstrate current and past positions, education (degrees, dates, thesis titles), awards, publications, professional activities, and foreign language competence. NEH considers the résumé primarily under criterion 4.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review Criterion 5: Likelihood of completion and dissemination
rubrics_metrics.description: The likelihood that the applicant will complete the project (not necessarily during the period of performance), including, when relevant, the soundness of the dissemination and access plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe intended audience, intended results, dissemination plans, publisher interest if any, and access (especially for digital products) in the Narrative under 'Final product and dissemination.' Explain long-term maintenance for digital outputs and any paywall plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative structure, content, and page limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Narrative must be succinct, well organized, free of technical terms and jargon, and not exceed three single-spaced pages with one-inch margins and font size no smaller than eleven points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize narrative under the headings: Significance and contribution; Organization and methods; Competencies, skills, and access; Final product and dissemination. Do not include an executive summary, cover page, or table of contents. Images, charts, diagrams, footnotes and endnotes are allowed if within page limit. Citations count toward page limits. Name file narrative.pdf.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work Plan format and requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Work plan must reflect major activities, be based on a full-time commitment for two consecutive months, and must not exceed one page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide timeline of activities and project dates that match SF-424. Discuss plans if project won’t be finished during stipend. Name file workplan.pdf. NEH will primarily consider the work plan under review criterion 3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bibliography expectations and page limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Bibliography should consist of primary and secondary sources related directly to the project and must not exceed one page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include works relevant to substance and methods to demonstrate knowledge of the field. NEH will primarily consider bibliography under review criterion 1. Any standard bibliographic format acceptable. Name file bibliography.pdf.

rubrics_metrics.name: Résumé requirements and page limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Résumé must not exceed two pages and should present evidence of applicant qualifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include current/past positions, education (degrees, dates, thesis/dissertation titles), awards and honors (with dates), publications (full citations), other relevant activities, and foreign language competence level. Name file resume.pdf.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editions/translations sample attachment rules
rubrics_metrics.description: If proposing an edition or translation, include up to two pages: one page sample of original text and one page of edited/translated version.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attachment must not exceed two pages and should be named sample.pdf. If translating to English where other translations exist, provide rationale for new translation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Database project sample attachment rules
rubrics_metrics.description: If proposing a database, provide a sample entry not exceeding one page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Name file database.pdf.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visual materials attachment rules
rubrics_metrics.description: If relevant, provide sample visual materials on a single page (multiple images allowed but on one page); convert to PDF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visual attachments must not exceed one page and must be PDF; common image formats are not accepted. Name file visual.pdf.

rubrics_metrics.name: Degree conferral documentation (conditional)
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have completed all degree requirements but degree has not been conferred by the application deadline, include a letter from the dean or department chair attesting you have satisfied degree requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Name file degreeconferral.pdf. This attachment is conditionally required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attachment file format and naming requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Each attachment must be a single PDF file and named exactly as specified (narrative.pdf, workplan.pdf, bibliography.pdf, resume.pdf, sample.pdf, database.pdf, visual.pdf, degreeconferral.pdf, delinquentdebt.pdf).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Grants.gov Attachments Form instructions precisely. Grants.gov will not accept files that do not meet technical requirements. NEH will reject applications with unexpected appendices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting standards for pages
rubrics_metrics.description: All attachments must be letter size (8½ x 11”), have at least one-inch margins, use a font size no smaller than 11-point, use a standard Roman font (e.g., Arial, Georgia, Helvetica, Times New Roman), and be single-spaced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any standard citation style is acceptable; citations count in page limits. NEH will not review applications that exceed mandatory page limits or deviate from formatting instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required/conditionally required/optional component rules
rubrics_metrics.description: NEH designates each application component as Required, Conditionally Required, or Optional and will not review applications missing any required or relevant conditionally required documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not include attachments other than those listed. Appendices allowed only as listed (attachments 5–7).

rubrics_metrics.name: Project title and abstract guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Project title should be brief (no more than 125 characters) and descriptive; project description (abstract) should be written for a non-specialist audience and not exceed 1,000 characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Successful titles are descriptive and easily understood. NEH may retitle funded projects for clarity. Project description will serve as the application abstract during review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: individuals only and previous NEH awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Summer Stipends awards are made only to individuals. Applicants who have previously held an NEH individual award (list of specific programs) are ineligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizations cannot apply. If stipend is paid through an institution, the institution must remit all NEH funds to the individual and may not claim indirect costs. You may compete concurrently with some programs but cannot accept two awards with overlapping periods of performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: citizenship and residency
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligible applicants are U.S. citizens (domestic or abroad) and foreign nationals who have lived in the U.S. or its jurisdictions for at least three years prior to the deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foreign nationals who take up permanent residence outside the U.S. between the deadline and end of period of performance forfeit eligibility. Temporary travel abroad is permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: currently enrolled students
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants currently enrolled in a degree-granting program are ineligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have satisfied all degree requirements and are awaiting conferral, you are eligible but must include a dean/chair letter attesting conferral status in Attachment 8.

rubrics_metrics.name: Faculty nomination requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Tenured or tenure-track faculty who teach full time at U.S. higher education institutions (that are not exempt) must be nominated by their institution to apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions may nominate one faculty member per deadline. Each institution must designate a nominating official (usually an academic VP or dean) and must conduct fair/open competitions. Applicants must include nominator name/email on NEH Supplemental Information for Individuals Form. NEH will email nominating official 7–10 days after the deadline; nominator must confirm online by October 11, 2024, or applicant will be ineligible unless exempt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemptions to nomination requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain applicants may apply without institutional nomination: independent scholars; U.S. citizens teaching at foreign institutions; non-tenure-track faculty; staff (not faculty) at higher ed institutions; community college faculty/staff; emeritus faculty; and faculty/staff at specified minority-serving institutions (AANAPISIs, ANNHIs, NASNTIs, PBIs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If claiming exemption based on institutional designation (e.g., AANAPISI), verify institutional status for that year. An independent scholar with an affiliation that would require nomination will be ruled ineligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit on multiple submissions and final validated submission rule
rubrics_metrics.description: If you submit multiple applications before the deadline, NEH will accept your last validated submission under the correct funding opportunity number as final.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submitting to wrong funding opportunity or making corrections is allowed, but only the last validated correct submission counts. Do not submit multiple applications to this notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concurrent fellowships/grants policy
rubrics_metrics.description: You may simultaneously hold fellowships or grants from organizations other than NEH (including sabbaticals and institutional grants) in support of the same project during their periods of performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may not hold two or more NEH individual awards with overlapping activities or overlapping periods of performance. NEH will not delay periods to accommodate overlaps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborative project rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Summer Stipends are designed primarily for individuals; awards may not be divided. Each collaborator seeking funding must submit a separate application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each collaborator must independently meet eligibility requirements, clearly explain division of labor and interdependence of contributions. Peer reviewers evaluate each application on its own merits. If collaborators seek joint institutional funding, consider the Collaborative Research program instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited project types and uses of funds
rubrics_metrics.description: Awards may not be used for development of teaching methods/theories, student research (including dissertations/theses), training/coursework, support for graduate student assistants, preparation/revision of textbooks, curriculum development, educational/technical impact assessments, inventories of collections, writing guidebooks/how-to/self-help, activities performed by federal entities/personnel, promotion of particular political/religious/ideological points of view, advocacy of specific public policies/legislation, lobbying, projects outside the humanities (including creation/performance of art; creative writing, autobiographies, memoirs, creative nonfiction; policy studies; and social science research that does not address humanistic questions or use humanistic methods).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications that include unallowable costs or activities may be judged nonresponsive and returned without review. See D6. Funding Restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indirect costs and institutional payment rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Indirect costs are unallowable for Summer Stipends. If stipend is paid through an institution, it must remit all NEH funds to the individual and may not take an institutional allowance or claim indirect costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may elect payment through an institution but institution cannot retain any portion of the award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission platform and registration timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications must be submitted via Grants.gov Workspace under funding opportunity 20240918-FT and applicants must complete SAM.gov and Grants.gov registration in advance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SAM.gov and Grants.gov registration may take several weeks; NEH will not grant deadline extensions because of registration delays. NEH recommends submitting 48 hours prior to deadline to correct technical errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strict enforcement of page limits and formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: NEH will not review applications that exceed mandatory page limits or deviate from specified formatting instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not include attachments other than required/conditionally required. eGMS cannot detect some errors (missing components or excess pages), so ensure all pieces comply before submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters of reference: encouragement and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are encouraged to solicit two letters of reference addressing the proposed project and ability to undertake it; references submit letters online and must do so by October 11, 2024.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide names, email addresses, affiliations for references on the NEH Supplemental Information for Individuals Form. NEH emails references two weeks after the deadline to prompt submission. Missing letters will not disqualify an application, but late letters may not be considered by reviewers. For translations, one letter must be from an expert in the project's language and address the quality of the sample translation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review process and reviewer constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: NEH uses peer reviewers with relevant expertise to evaluate eligible and complete applications using the stated review criteria; reviewers must comply with federal conflicts-of-interest rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NEH staff review for eligibility/completeness, program officers may supplement reviewer comments, funding recommendations go to the National Council on the Humanities and final funding decisions are made by the Chair. Applicants may request copies of peer reviewers’ evaluations after announcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk assessment and pre-award requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: NEH Office of Grant Management conducts a risk assessment for selected applications considering past performance, eligibility, and compliance with public policy; OGM may request additional information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OGM may impose special terms and conditions or determine award levels. NEH may not issue awards to applicants with management/financial instability affecting compliance (2 CFR § 200.206).

rubrics_metrics.name: Award notice and acceptance process
rubrics_metrics.description: If selected, NEH Office of Grant Management will send award documents through eGMS Reach beginning in April 2025 and recipients must complete NEH Individual Programs Acceptance Form to establish payment schedule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notification email in April 2025 is not authorization to begin performance or incur costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting requirement: final performance report
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must submit a final performance report within 120 calendar days after the period of performance ends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report collects information on accomplishments, outcomes/outputs, other financial support, impact, and acknowledgement of NEH support. Submit online via eGMS Reach. A final financial report is not required. NEH assesses recipients based on outputs described in proposal; recipients are encouraged to send copies of resulting books and update eGMS Reach 'Products and Prizes' tab.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public access and digital preservation expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: NEH prefers projects that provide free access to the public and expects digital materials produced to be maintained for long-term availability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how public will access digital materials and how they will be maintained beyond the period of performance. If paywall is planned, explain rationale and impacts on access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright and NEH retained rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may copyright work developed under the award, subject to NEH’s royalty-free, nonexclusive, irrevocable right to reproduce, publish, or otherwise use the work for federal purposes (2 CFR § 200.315(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NEH typically consults recipients when exercising rights and may publish excerpts in Humanities magazine or on its website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Debarment, suspension, and delinquent federal debt rules
rubrics_metrics.description: NEH will not process awards for individuals with delinquent federal debt or who have been suspended, debarred, declared ineligible, or voluntarily excluded; applicants must comply with 2 CFR §§ 180.335 and .350.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you cannot attest to statements in the certification, include Attachment 9: Explanation of delinquent federal debt (delinquentdebt.pdf) and provide evidence of repayment arrangements if applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geospatial data due diligence
rubrics_metrics.description: If requesting funds for geospatial data/products/services, you must search Data.gov to determine whether needed data already exist and, if not, produce proposed geospatial products in compliance with Federal Geographic Data Committee guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform due diligence search before requesting NEH funds for geospatial activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: NEH termination rights and reporting of misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: NEH reserves the right to terminate awards consistent with 2 CFR § 200.340 and expects reporting of allegations of waste, fraud, abuse, mismanagement, or research misconduct to its Office of the Inspector General.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review NEH Research Misconduct Policy and report concerns to the NEH OIG as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application completeness enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: NEH will not consider incomplete, nonresponsive, or ineligible applications for funding and will not consider applications submitted after the deadline except under rare late submission policy cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure all required and conditionally required components are included and formatted; check Grants.gov and eGMS statuses and correct technical errors prior to deadline.
